evidence: Egress resources are a deliberate cross-service boundary: agentplane/policy_controller/internal/controller/account_use.go imports agentplane/egress/resources.Placeholder; BUILD grants only that controller package as the exception to Egress subpackage visibility.

The sidecar is a separate deployed binary with no Go importers; its go_library and binary are already restricted to //agentplane/egress:__pkg__. Its location documents the separate runtime alongside sidecar_config.py/platform_routes.py, and egress/README.md describes the split.
The existing internal packages already align with runtime responsibilities; EgressAdmin and EgressRules have prior accepted moves and are excluded.
retain_decisions.decision: Retain. Internalizing resources would break a real policy-controller boundary. Moving the sidecar would add Bazel labels/runfile-path churn without changing its already restricted ownership or public API.
retain_decisions.invariants: Keep API/resource interpretation, Egress placeholder derivation, and independent sidecar deployment/configuration boundaries intact.

evidence: The five Go service files share package main and form one binary/configuration/handler boundary. No other package imports the implementation import path; Runtime imports the generated llm_ingress/v1 ModelConfig proto contract instead.

codex_catalog.go is a small in-memory catalog loader consumed only by ingressHandler; model_config.go is the service's implementation of its generated RPC. Splitting either would create a helper package without a separate owner.
retain_decisions.decision: Retain the service implementation together and keep the versioned proto as the shared contract; no additional ownership boundary is justified.
retain_decisions.invariants: Preserve request authentication, attribution, proxy behavior, Codex catalog response/ETag, and ModelConfig RPC semantics.

evidence: The root Firecracker API/VMM/guest lifecycle files form the host-side VM owner and are consumed by agentplane/env/firecracker; the root BUILD intentionally exposes them only to Agentplane subpackages.

vsock already separates the host/guest stream protocol and restricts BUILD visibility to the two direct Firecracker owners. workloadidentity separately owns the guest Workload API server/PEM parsing. launcher and runtime_probe are standalone command/test tools.
retain_decisions.decision: Retain existing split. Further splitting API, guest management, credentials, and VM supervision would cut across one guest-start/credential-delivery lifecycle and require new package APIs without a distinct owner.
retain_decisions.invariants: Keep boot identity verification, credential delivery, guest synchronization, VMM ownership, vsock framing and shutdown behavior unchanged.

evidence: Current package responsibilities already identify the main data and RPC owners. settledcursors is an 82-line leaf used by both internal/projection and internal/threadfold; it centralizes cursor-range semantics rather than belonging to one consumer.

threadfold owns event-to-Thread folding and golden fixtures; projection consumes it. storage owns the transactional raw-history/settlement store; ingress and rpc own separate server surfaces. backfill and ops are operational tools, not service implementation subpackages.
retain_decisions.decision: Retain current owners; no useful consolidation or split remains in this audit scope.
retain_decisions.invariants: Keep append/settlement transaction boundaries, cursor coverage semantics, lease ownership, projection epoch behavior, and ingress caller revalidation with their existing owners.

retain_decisions.area: Public Sandbox client/config SDK and shared support
evidence: environmentruntimeclient is genuinely shared by Runner Gateway Dispatcher, Sandbox Controller, Notification, and App bridge; sandboxes is the common domain owner, while moving it beneath any one consumer would reverse ownership.

runtimeconfig is the deployment-published model/harness/template contract shared by App, Action orchestration, Runner Gateway, and cdk8s; the App README documents that external contract. It is intentionally separate from service-specific settings.

net/grpc/postgres/identity packages are individually named by their shared capability. postgres/wakeups has cross-service production importers, whereas postgres/lease is a distinct database primitive from sandboxes/lease. testing/postgres is explicitly testonly and shared across integration targets; x packages remain experimental by location.
retain_decisions.decision: Retain these shared boundaries. Moving them under a single consuming service or broad common package would make ownership less accurate; no extra refactor group recommended.
retain_decisions.invariants: Preserve shared per-RPC token/transport behavior, deployment-published configuration semantics, wakeup fan-out/reconnect signals, lease ownership, and test-only fixture boundaries.
